title: Federated Learning for Misbehaviour Detection with Variational Autoencoders and Gaussian Mixture Models
multi_agent_setting: each vehicle is an FL client; cloud aggregator (Fed+) and shared repository of misbehaviour events
problem: unsupervised misbehaviour detection without centralising BSMs
method: VAE + GMM per vehicle, RBM pre-training, Fed+ aggregation for non-IID clients
metrics_result: detection performance > 80% (abstract), better than supervised FL baselines with artificial splits
limitation_gap: per-message features, no trajectory/sequence representation; Sybil identity linking not addressed
relevance_why: unsupervised FL on VeReMi; closest FL analogue of our one-class AE baselines

title: Distributed Federated Learning for Vehicular Network Security: Anomaly Detection Benefits and Multi-Domain Attack Threats
multi_agent_setting: vehicles exchange models with one-hop neighbours, multi-hop propagation, no server
problem: misbehaviour classification where local data is scarce
method: distributed (peer-to-peer) FL of deep classifiers; also jamming and data poisoning threats
metrics_result: accuracy gains over local-only learning, largest for low-accuracy vehicles (no single headline number in abstract)
limitation_gap: supervised, labels assumed at every vehicle; message-level classifier; no split-by-vehicle leakage discussion
relevance_why: uses VeReMi Extension and receiver-local data, matching our receiver-view prepared data

title: Targeted Attacks and Defenses for Distributed Federated Learning in Vehicular Networks
multi_agent_setting: vehicles as DFL peers, some adversarial (poisoning / backdoor)
problem: robustness of serverless FL to targeted poisoning and Trojans
method: design targeted poisoning + backdoor attacks on DFL, propose defenses
metrics_result: DFL more robust than individual learning (qualitative)
limitation_gap: no quantitative result in abstract; dataset unstated
relevance_why: adversarial agents inside collaborative detection; background only

title: Knowledge Transfer for Collaborative Misbehavior Detection in Untrusted Vehicular Environments
multi_agent_setting: roadside units as learning agents sharing knowledge; some RSUs compromised
problem: collaborative detection among RSUs when some sources are untrusted
method: deep RL + transfer learning, selective transfer only from trustworthy source RSUs; label-flipping and policy-induction attacks
dataset_simulator: open-source MBD dataset (name not on abstract page)
metrics_result: lower training time at target RSU, better detection than tabula rasa, generalises to unseen attacks
limitation_gap: RSU-level; per-message time series; Sybil pseudonym linking not studied
relevance_why: multi-RSU collaboration with untrusted peers; transfer to unseen attacks parallels our held-out DataReplay

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Misbehavior Detection in Vehicular Networks
multi_agent_setting: RSU processes V2X data broadcast by vehicles (single RL agent at RSU)
problem: classify incoming V2X data as misbehaving or genuine
method: RL-based detector on time-series at RSUs
dataset_simulator: open-source dataset (reported recall 0.997, F1 0.9845 per secondary summary)
metrics_result: recall 0.9970, F1 0.9845 (from search summary of abstract)
limitation_gap: single agent; no Sybil-specific analysis
relevance_why: time-series MBD at RSU; precursor of the collaborative RSU work

title: MistralBSM: Leveraging Mistral-7B for Vehicular Networks Misbehavior Detection
multi_agent_setting: edge LLM at vehicle/edge + larger cloud LLM validating (two-tier agents)
problem: misbehaviour detection from BSM sequences
method: fine-tuned Mistral-7B (0.012% parameters updated) on BSM sequences as text; cloud LLM verification
metrics_result: 98% binary / 96% multiclass accuracy; beats LLaMA2-7B and RoBERTa
limitation_gap: selected attacks only; accuracy on imbalanced data; leakage of split by vehicle not discussed; latency of 7B model
relevance_why: LLM over BSM sequences on VeReMi = direct comparator for sequence models and an LLM-agent idea

title: Credibility Enhanced Temporal Graph Convolutional Network Based Sybil Attack Detection On Edge Computing Servers
multi_agent_setting: edge servers (RSUs) build graphs of nearby vehicles; global credibility shared across ECSs via Bayesian inference
problem: Sybil vehicles overloading edge computing servers
method: temporal GCN (GCN + GRU) on vehicle connectivity graphs + Bayesian credibility across servers
metrics_result: identifies most Sybil vehicles at low error rate (qualitative)
limitation_gap: own simulated data; not evaluated on VeReMi; privacy-driven topology features
relevance_why: graph over identities across time, multi-server credibility; candidate for Sybil detection on VeReMi GridSybil

title: Enhancing Security in VANETs with Efficient Sybil Attack Detection using Fog Computing
multi_agent_setting: onboard units of vehicles in a region form a dynamic fog that jointly detects rogue nodes
problem: Sybil detection without RSUs
method: FSDV: vehicular fog computing over neighbouring OBUs
metrics_result: 43% lower processing delay, 13% lower overhead, 35% lower FPR at high density vs existing schemes
limitation_gap: own simulation; text overlap with the authors' other preprints (noted on arXiv)
relevance_why: vehicles as cooperating detectors for Sybil

title: Detecting Sybil Attacks using Proofs of Work and Location in VANETs
multi_agent_setting: RSUs issue location proofs; vehicles submit trajectories; detector matches trajectories
problem: limit and detect Sybil identities
method: RSU-signed location proofs + proof-of-work; Sybil trajectories found as cliques of overlapping trajectories
metrics_result: high detection rate, low false negatives (qualitative)
limitation_gap: needs RSU infrastructure and protocol change; not usable on passive message logs
relevance_why: trajectory-overlap idea is the same signal GridSybil ghosts leave in VeReMi

title: Collaborative Learning Based Sybil Attack Detection in Vehicular AD-HOC Networks (VANETS)

relevance_why: Sybil-specific baseline but weak multi-agent content
